titleText.es: LOS ESTUDIANTES ESTÁN LLAMANDO AL PRESIDENTE JOHNSON EN MASA PARA PROTESTAR POR EL BOMBARDEO Y HAN COLAPSADO LA CENTRALITA DE LA CASA BLANCA.¿PODRÍAN COLAPSAR NUESTROS SISTEMAS TELEFÓNICOS CRÍTICOS? ¿HA COMENZADO LA PRIMERA GUERRA TELEFÓNICA? PERMANEZCAN A LA ESCUCHA PARA SABER MÁS SOBRE ESTA NUEVA Y PELIGROSA TECNOLOGÍA.
titleText.en: STUDENTS ARE CALLING PRESIDENT JOHNSON EN MASSE TO PROTEST THE BOMBING AND IT'S JAMMED THE WHITE HOUSE SWITCHBOARD. COULD THEY COLLAPSE OUR CRITICAL PHONE SYSTEMS? HAS THE FIRST TELEPHONE WAR BEGUN? STAY TUNED FOR MORE ON THIS DANGEROUS NEW TECHNOLOGY.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and English texts are the exact title attributes from the Spanish archive and official xkcd. The browser URL, organization names, acronym, personal name, and leading punctuation reaction are audited exclusions. Window controls, navigation icons, the download icon, search icon, globe, figures, and speech tails are structural artwork. Leak remains a lexical English borrowing inside the Spanish phrase NUEVO LEAK.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A legión was originally a large military unit. It can also describe a very numerous, organized, or devoted group.

example.es: Una legión de seguidores esperaba fuera.
example.en: A legion of followers was waiting outside.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Standalone todos can refer to all the people in a group. It is masculine plural for an all-male or mixed group; todas is used for an all-female group.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we are (at a place or location)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estamos is the form of estar used with nosotros, ‘we.’ Use it for where a group is; somos instead gives an identity or defining description.

example.en: We have been here since early.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: information leak; unauthorized release of information
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish technology and media writing sometimes borrows English leak informally. It is normally treated as a masculine noun: un leak, el leak.

example.es: El periodista investigó un leak de documentos.
example.en: The journalist investigated a leak of documents.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nombres is the plural of nombre. It can refer to personal names, labels, or the names assigned to things.

example.es: La lista contiene nombres y fechas.
example.en: The list contains names and dates.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Direcciones can mean addresses or directions. With names and phone numbers, it refers to contact or location addresses.

example.es: Guardaron las direcciones de los clientes.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bajar literally means to lower or go down. On websites and in informal technology language, it can mean to download a file; descargar is another common choice.

example.es: Puedes bajar el archivo desde la página.
example.en: You can download the file from the page.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: luchar por + causa, persona u objetivo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone fights for or works hard in support of a cause or goal?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of luchar, then por, then name the cause, person, or goal.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por introduces what the effort supports or seeks to defend. If the goal is an action, luchar por can instead be followed by the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.

example.es: Luchan por la libertad de expresión.
example.en: They fight for freedom of expression.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say phone number or phone numbers?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use número de teléfono for one and números de teléfono for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Número changes between singular and plural. De teléfono identifies the kind of number and stays unchanged in both forms.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why can a button or menu item use an unchanged dictionary-form verb as an instruction?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Spanish interfaces often use a verb's unchanged dictionary form to name the action the control performs.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This unchanged form is called the infinitive and usually ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. It is not addressed to tú or usted here; it functions as a short action label, especially on buttons, menus, notices, and lists of instructions.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: legión · nadie y todos · leak de identidades · maldita sea
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why is the published leak especially damaging to the Anonymous speaker?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The group presents itself as a vast anonymous collective, but the leak publishes members' identifying and contact information.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Anonymous became associated with collective slogans and concealed individual identities. WikiLeaks became known for publishing leaked material. The page therefore turns the transparency model against Anonymous itself, and the final speaker identified as Julian reacts in frustration.
